messages:
andrea: Hey team — noticing steady memory growth on a Dedicated worker when serving long-context workloads with continuous batching. Over ~30m RSS climbed ~1.8x and we hit one OOM near the end. Suspect interaction between batch-merge heuristics and KV pager (paging/eviction + fragmentation). Anyone else seen this pattern?

michael: I saw something similar on canary yesterday, but chalked it up to a quant regression. I saved a perf trace: https://perf.internal/trace/1978899000 (flamegraph + heatmap).

sasha: Can you paste the evict logs? curious if kernel selection (fp16 vs int8 path) is changing allocation sizes and affecting slab fragmentation.

devon: paste of recent logs from the worker: 
```
KVPager: want_pages=6 pages_avail=2 evict_attempts=3 evicted=0 pages_needed=4 thrash_count=12
KVCache: fragment_count=342 free_slots=128 avg_slot_size=512
BatchMerge: merged_from=3 -> merged_size=28 head_wait_ms=42
```

andrea: thanks. The batch merge heuristic currently: if inter-arrival < 12ms and batch_size < 16 then merge. With long contexts many requests keep KV hits high and we form very large merged batches that hold onto KV slices while waiting for tailing ops -> head-of-line blocking. That plus the pager struggling to evict contiguous ranges seems to cause the memory spiral.

jia: Proposed quick tweak: make merge window adaptive by avg_context_len and recent_kv_hits. e.g., pseudo: 
```
if avg_kv_hits(reqs_in_window) > KV_HIT_THRESH:
  merge_window_ms = max(6, base_window_ms/2)
else:
  merge_window_ms = base_window_ms
```
This should reduce creating huge merged batches for long-chat sessions.

sasha: Also add a metric: per-batch kv_occupancy_ratio = bytes_present / bytes_reserved and pgfault_rate. If occupancy_ratio stays high while pgfault_rate increases -> pager can't keep up. Grafana query suggestion: `sum(rate(kv_pager_evictions[1m])) by (worker)` and `histogram_quantile(0.95, rate(batch_latency_bucket[5m]))`

perf-bot: automated profile uploaded: top functions: kv_pager_reclaim 42%, merge_batch_wait 18%, kv_slot_coalesce 9%. Saved as: https://perf.internal/1978901200/summary

michael: I ran the stress harness locally to try to repro. Command: `./tools/stress_client --scenario long_ctx_contbatch --qps 120 --ctx 16k --duration 45m`. After ~20m fragmentation grows and RSS steps up in ~500MB increments on merges. Repro logs: https://internal/artefacts/repro/1978901210.log

andrea: Plan: implement an adaptive merge backoff that reduces merge aggressiveness when avg_kv_hits > 0.6 or when pager_evictions/sec > 5. Will also add a temporary guard to cap merged_batch_size to 12 for long-context tenants. I'll open a PR and roll to staging canary. Can volunteers watch memory and pager metrics and OOM alerts?

devon: I can watch. I'll also add a unit test in perf-suite that simulates rapid merge/split cycles and checks fragmentation delta.

ops-bot: Deployment scheduled: patch/kvcache-adaptive-merge -> staging at 2026-03-18T18:40:00Z. Notified on-call.

andrea: thanks — posting follow-up once canary runs. If this looks good we can iterate on kernel selection knobs next (kernel-fallback for slow paths) and maybe a background defragmenter that coalesces free slabs during idle CPU windows.
